name: GA-14
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+19 district with a Republican incumbent and an R-favorable national environment
Prediction markets price a Democratic win at only about 4%
Harris raised $8.4M to Fuller's $2.1M but has little cash left and minimal outside backing
No public polls or expert ratings; the race rests on fundamentals
model.rationale: The district's deep Republican lean, Fuller's incumbency, and a Republican-favorable environment make him a strong favorite, and markets agree. Harris's exceptional fundraising narrows the expected margin only modestly, since most is already spent and outside groups have put far more money behind Fuller.
model.watch: Late polling or a wave of Democratic outside spending showing Harris within single digits would be the main signal of movement toward a closer race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Georgia's 14th District is one of the most Republican-leaning seats in the country, with a partisan lean of R+19. Incumbent Clay Fuller, renominated without difficulty, seeks another term against Democrat Shawn Harris. The national environment favors Republicans this cycle, adding to Fuller's structural advantage, and prediction markets give Democrats only about a four percent chance of an upset.

Harris has run an unusually well-funded campaign, raising roughly $8.4 million to Fuller's $2.1 million, though most of that money has been spent, and outside groups have put more than $2.7 million behind Fuller against modest spending on Harris's behalf. No public polls or expert ratings are available for this race. The combination of district lean, incumbency, and environment makes Fuller a strong favorite, with Harris's fundraising the main source of residual uncertainty.
